notes: §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR5: 'Data-name-2 may be qualified and must be a numeric elementary item representing an integer.' ScreenPositionOperandClass refuses a non-numeric data-name at every edition (COBOL0844), and at 85, where the subscript-arithmetic-expression-2002 construct is unavailable, ScreenCobol85SubscriptDataNames (called from ReadSubscripts) refuses a data-name with digit positions right of the point (COBOL0900), while Cobol85OperandForms.IsSubscript keeps the shape to data-name [{+|-} integer]. Probes at --std 85 (work-rd-04/c7): refused: PIC X (the witness), numeric edited Z9, a group, USAGE INDEX item, PIC 9V9 and PIC P9 (scale > 0), S9 * 2, S9 + SS, FUNCTION INTEGER(S9), ((S9)), a ref-modified SSS (18:1), empty parentheses (COBOL2309); accepted with the right element: PIC 9, signed S9, COMP, PACKED-DECIMAL, PIC 9P (value 10 -> J), S9(18), elementary SG1, qualified SQN OF SR / SQN IN SQ (H / G), S9 + 1 and S9 - 1, and an ODO table subscripted by its DEPENDING item. At 2023 the 9V9 and expression forms are accepted (edition arm). Lead for the general-format row, not SR5: a subscripted data-name-2, ELT (STE (1)), is accepted at 85 (prints B), though §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.2 prints data-name-2 bare; IsSubscript admits any dataReference. || The level-66 RENAMES alias of a numeric integer item (§1985:VI.5.11.4 GR2: "all of the data attributes of data-name-2") is read as the renamed item: SubscriptBinder.ResolveSubscriptName substitutes RenamesInfo.From for a no-THROUGH alias and PositionRead declines a level-66 item so the segment reroutes to the D18 place route (kb/Work PB5477, witness 1985-SR-IV_4_3_8_2_3-5-renames-alias).

next.reason: 1985 requires at compile time that the subscript data-name-2 'must be a numeric elementary item representing an integer'. In 2023 a subscript is arithmetic-expression-1 (§2023:8.4.2.3.2), whose identifiers need only reference a numeric data item (uncataloged §2023:8.8.1.1, 'an identifier referencing a numeric data item'), qualified as needed. A non-integer is no longer refused: §2023:8.4.2.3.4 GR1 says 'does not result in an integer, the EC-BOUND-SUBSCRIPT exception condition is set to exist'. A compile-time refusal became a run-time exception condition (error mode c). Integer subscripts in conforming 1985 programs behave the same.
